**What you should be able to do after this meeting.** Write an identification section that names your design, its assumption, and what would break it. State a limitation without gutting your own project.

## Before class

**Reading.** TBD

The opening quiz is on this reading.

## Session A · 2:05–3:15

Academic writing III — the design paper. The same method on a harder object. You outlined this two weeks ago, so today is what the identification section has to contain. The graph you drew in meeting 8. Your design, named. Its assumption, stated. And what would break it. Then how to state a limitation without gutting your own project. Then reading for the skeleton one last time: what a referee actually looks for, which is how you will write your own referee report. If you cannot reconstruct a paper's outline, that is the finding. Finally reproducibility at awareness level. Where files live. Naming. What 'the final version' means. And when version control is worth the cost.

## Session B · 3:35–4:30

Every session B opens with a ten-minute team check-in: what you did
since last week, what is stuck, and who is doing what next. Written
down, and handed in with that session's work.

Bring your sketch — topic sentences with the evidence noted under each, not prose. Workshop it in rotation. Somebody else reads your skeleton and tells you where the argument jumps. Then each team presents its design and the assumption it is defending. Then you rate your teammates for the second time.

Your team's output is submitted before you leave.

## Due

Design paper — sketch, marked up in class · Present your design · Rate your teammates · Exercise 2 — rebuild and critique a figure, end of week
